records.title: Release notes overview
records.relevance_note: Official runtime mechanisms for tool search, tool calling, and context compaction.
records.reason_included: Concrete provider-level mechanisms for on-demand tool loading and token control.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Programmatic tool calling lets Claude call tools from within code execution to reduce latency and token usage in multi-tool workflows.
The tool search tool enables Claude to dynamically discover and load tools on-demand from large tool catalogs.
Client-side compaction in the Python and TypeScript SDK tool_runner automatically manages conversation context through summarization.
Web search and web fetch can be dynamically filtered using code execution before results reach the context window, improving performance and reducing token costs.

records.title: Tools
records.relevance_note: Protocol-level mechanics for listing, paging, and invalidating tool catalogs.
records.reason_included: Defines the base discovery and cache-invalidation contract many MCP agents depend on.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Servers that support dynamic tool updates advertise a tools capability with listChanged set to true.
The tools/list request supports pagination using an optional cursor parameter.
Servers SHOULD send notifications/tools/list_changed when the available tool list changes.

claim_locations.locator: Section 'List Changed Notification', protocol notification definition

records.title: Changelog / MCP tool search auto mode default
records.relevance_note: Official threshold rule for deferring MCP tool descriptions.
records.reason_included: Direct operational rule for when tool descriptions stay out of the main context.

claim_snippets.claim_text: MCP tool search auto mode is enabled by default.
When MCP tool descriptions exceed 10% of the context window, Claude Code defers them and discovers tools via MCPSearch instead of loading all descriptions up front.
Users can disable this behavior by adding MCPSearch to disallowedTools.

records.title: API changelog / Tool search in Responses API
records.relevance_note: Official launch note tying runtime tool search to token, cache, and latency tradeoffs.
records.reason_included: Concrete provider statement about deferring large tool surfaces until runtime.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Tool search in the Responses API lets models defer large tool surfaces until runtime.
OpenAI states that this reduces token usage, preserves cache performance, and improves latency.
The same release introduced native Compaction support for longer-running agent workflows.

records.title: App Server
records.relevance_note: Operational endpoints for listing app/plugin/MCP availability and restoring dynamic tools.
records.reason_included: Concrete interface for surfacing auth state and tool status outside the prompt.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The app server exposes plugin/list, app/list, mcpServer/oauth/login, config/mcpServer/reload, and mcpServerStatus/list methods; mcpServerStatus/list includes MCP servers, tools, resources, and auth status.
If an enabled required MCP server fails to initialize, thread start and resume fail instead of continuing without it.
Dynamic tools are persisted on thread metadata and restored on resume.
skills/list may return a cached result, and forceReload:true refreshes it; if a skill item is omitted, the model may still try to locate it, adding latency.

records.title: MCP
records.exception_reason: Defines foundational MCP allowlist and approval-control primitives that later runtime tool-search systems build on.
records.relevance_note: Foundational API controls for limiting an MCP server's visible tools and approval flow.
records.reason_included: Concrete low-level controls for progressive exposure and approval gating.

claim_snippets.claim_text: An MCP server tool configuration can specify an allowed_tools array to expose only selected tools from that server.
The same configuration can set require_approval for that MCP server.
The configuration binds tool exposure to a named remote server instance via server_label and server_url.

records.title: Changelog / Team Config for shared configuration
records.relevance_note: Dated file-backed configuration layering for shared skills and constraints.
records.reason_included: Operational detail for deterministic tool and skill exposure from workspace and user scopes.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Team Config shares config.toml defaults, rules, and skills across repositories and machines.
Codex loads .codex/ configuration from the current working directory, parent folders, the repo root, and user and system locations.
Higher-precedence locations override lower-precedence ones, while requirements.toml can enforce constraints regardless of location.

records.title: When tool descriptions exceed 10% of context they should be loaded via search, but are still getting added to context
records.relevance_note: Field report showing a documented threshold rule not being enforced in practice.
records.reason_included: Useful failure case for dynamic tool loading thresholds and observability.

claim_snippets.claim_text: In the reported reproduction, /context showed MCP tools consuming 28.1k tokens, or 14.1% of the context window.
Despite being above the stated 10% threshold, the MCP tool descriptions were still loaded into context instead of being deferred to search.
The issue reproducer explicitly tied the mismatch to the new MCP tool search auto mode behavior announced the same day.

records.title: MCP tools taking too much context
records.relevance_note: MCP tools taking too much context is a issue thread source with details on context metering, tool menu bloat relevant to tooling tool gateway.
records.reason_included: Included for source-local evidence on tool gateway, context, cost budget.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The reporter's /doctor output showed MCP tools context at about 144,802 tokens, well above the low-context warning threshold.
One MCP provider contributed 135 tools and about 125,964 tokens by itself.
Another provider contributed 26 tools and about 17,512 tokens.

records.title: After MCP auth, tool provider list API still returns stale data from Redis cache
records.relevance_note: Shows auth completion and tool-availability state diverging because cached provider status was not refreshed.
records.reason_included: Concrete auth-state and tool-status surfacing failure.

claim_snippets.claim_text: After completing MCP auth, the tool_providers list API still returned stale data from Redis cache.
The UI continued to show the server as not authenticated even though the authentication flow had completed.
Expected behavior was an authenticated provider with tools listed, but actual behavior was unauthenticated with no tools displayed.

records.title: Claude sees stale tools after tools/list_changed notification
records.relevance_note: Claude sees stale tools after tools/list_changed notification is a issue thread source with details on list changed invalidation, dynamic tool catalog relevant to tooling tool gateway.
records.reason_included: Included for source-local evidence on tool gateway, state, execution loop.

claim_snippets.claim_text: After notifications/tools/list_changed, the client requested tools/list and the server returned N+1 tools.
Claude still reported only the old N tools and could not invoke the newly-added tool.
Disconnecting and reconnecting was the workaround that refreshed the visible tool list.

claim_snippets.claim_text: A large toolResult message was appended directly to the transcript and pushed the next prompt over the model's token limit.
The report cites a roughly 560k-character JSON line at transcript line 1403 followed by a prompt-too-long error on line 1404: 205607 tokens > 200000.
The run did not automatically compact or otherwise recover before sending the next model request.

records.title: ToolReAGt: Tool Retrieval for LLM-based Complex Task Solution via Retrieval Augmented Generation
records.exception_reason: Establishes an early empirical baseline for using ReAct for iterative tool retrieval to combat tool bloat prior to the widespread adoption of MCP-based dynamic retrieval standards.
records.relevance_note: Demonstrates that dynamically querying for tool definitions using a dedicated reasoning step significantly outperforms stuffing all tools into the context.
records.reason_included: Concrete ablation showing an 8.9% recall improvement by deferring tool context injection until an explicit sub-task demands it.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Using ReAct prompting for iterative tool retrieval, identifying if a tool is required before associating it with sub-tasks, improved recall@5 by 8.9% on the UltraTool benchmark over direct n-best RAG.

records.title: ScaleMCP: Dynamic and Auto-Synchronizing Model Context Protocol Tools for LLM Agents
records.exception_reason: Provides foundational mechanisms for auto-synchronizing MCP tool availability dynamically at runtime and introduces targeted embeddings for tool descriptions.
records.relevance_note: Focuses on maintaining accurate tool state synchronization when the set of MCP tools changes dynamically.
records.reason_included: Extracts the mechanism of using the MCP server as the single source of truth for tool availability rather than maintaining a monolithic static list.

claim_snippets.claim_text: ScaleMCP equips LLM agents with an auto-synchronizing tool storage pipeline using CRUD operations to maintain MCP servers as the single source of truth, avoiding inconsistencies from monolithic local tool repositories.
The Tool Document Weighted Average (TDWA) embedding strategy selectively emphasizes critical components like tool names and synthetic questions during embedding to improve retrieval accuracy.

claim_locations.locator: Abstract, final sentence on TDWA embeddings
Introduction, first paragraph on CRUD-based tool synchronization

records.title: Model Context Protocol and the 'too many tools' problem
records.exception_reason: Documents specific hard-limit failure modes and token consumption metrics for early MCP clients like Cursor and Copilot before dynamic retrieval frameworks were adopted.
records.relevance_note: A practical exploration of the token bloat introduced by raw MCP tool registration.
records.reason_included: Captures the real-world fallback mechanisms (hard limits and truncation) implemented by IDE agents when dynamic tool prefetch isn't available.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Exposing too many MCP tools directly crowds the context window, with GitHub Copilot enforcing a hard limit of 128 tools and Cursor strictly truncating after 40 MCP tools to prevent prompt bloat.

records.title: Tools Are Under-Documented: Simple Document Expansion Boosts Tool Retrieval
records.relevance_note: Addresses the root cause of dynamic tool retrieval failures: mismatched semantics between user intent and minimal technical API docs.
records.reason_included: Highlights that prefetching fails without systemic expansion of tool documentation, providing a concrete `tool_profile` mechanism to fix it.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The primary bottleneck in dynamic tool retrieval is poor documentation quality and structural inconsistency, not model capability. Expanding tool metadata with a structured tool_profile systematically bridges the semantic gap with user queries.

claim_locations.locator: Opening analysis of optimization objectives and shutdown as an obstacle, paragraph 5

records.title: Why dynamic tool discovery solves the context management problem
records.relevance_note: Directly explains the mechanism of deferring tool injection using a search primitive to avoid upfront context limits.
records.reason_included: Contains highly specific quantitative data on the token cost of static MCP tool definitions vs dynamic retrieval overhead.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Marking tools with `defer_loading: true` allows the model to only see a search primitive and core tools initially; when the search primitive is called, only the 3-5 returned `tool_reference` objects are expanded into full schemas.
Static full catalog injection of 50 MCP tools consumes approximately 72K to 77K tokens before task execution, whereas dynamic selection drops this overhead to roughly 8.7K tokens.

claim_locations.locator: Section 'Why dynamic tool discovery solves the context management problem'
Section 'Why Static Full Catalog Injection Breaks at Scale'

records.title: Dynamic tool discovery in MCP
records.relevance_note: A prime example of state-driven dynamic tool prefetch, hiding invalid tools without client restarts.
records.reason_included: Extracts the exact MCP primitive (`notifications/tools/list_changed`) used to manage state-driven tool availability.

claim_snippets.claim_text: When tool authentication expires, the MCP server can dynamically hide specific tools (e.g., `getWhatsAppChatById`) by emitting a `notifications/tools/list_changed` message, prompting the client to fetch an updated tool list without reconnecting.

claim_locations.locator: Dynamic tool discovery in MCP section

records.title: MCP vs mcp-cli: Dynamic Tool Discovery for Token-Efficient AI Agents
records.relevance_note: Provides architectural validation from Microsoft on dynamically fetching tool contexts over static loading.
records.reason_included: Showcases a dedicated terminal tooling layer (`mcp-cli`) that handles connection pooling and lazy context discovery specifically to bypass multi-server MCP bloat.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Using `mcp-cli` introduces dynamic context discovery via lazy loading and connection pooling, pulling in tool definitions only when needed to prevent context window bloat when integrating multiple MCP servers.

claim_locations.locator: Part 2: Enter mcp-cli – Dynamic Context Discovery

records.title: Leveraging the MCP Registry in Kong Konnect for Dynamic Tool Discovery
records.relevance_note: Shows an enterprise architecture for multi-server dynamic tool prefetching via a central registry.
records.reason_included: Extracts the registry pattern where tool discovery is decoupled from the agent; the agent queries the registry, extracts the target URL, and binds the tool on the fly.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Separating tool discovery from execution through an MCP Registry allows the agent to first search the registry, dynamically parse the returned URL to configure the MCP server connection, and then execute the action without hardcoded integrations.

claim_locations.locator: Building an agent that uses the MCP Registry section

records.title: When Too Many Tools Become Too Much Context: A Deep Dive into RAG-MCP
records.relevance_note: A focused writeup quantifying exact failure points when dumping tools into context limits.
records.reason_included: Extracts concrete measured thresholds for when static tool injection fails (at ~30 tools) and the severity of the drop-off.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Tool selection accuracy exceeds 90% when the candidate pool is under 30 tools, but drops sharply to approximately 13.62% as the tool pool scales into the hundreds due to context rot.

claim_locations.locator: The Numbers Tell the Story section

records.title: A Practical Approach to Smart Tool Retrieval for Enterprise AI Agents
records.relevance_note: A highly detailed two-stage architecture for solving prefetch vs latency tradeoffs in dynamic tool retrieval.
records.reason_included: Captures the interaction effect of candidate pruning followed by interaction-aware reranking to accurately filter a large catalog of available tools down to the prompt.

claim_snippets.claim_text: A retrieve-then-refine framework using Tool2Vec for fast candidate pruning and a ToolRefiner model to analyze inter-tool and query interactions improved tool retrieval recall by up to 30.5% on the ToolBank dataset.
